title: Evidence notice: a one-off exclusion gives a spurious restricted-then-lifted notice pair
outcome: Evidence notice: a one-off exclusion gives a spurious restricted-then-lifted notice pair
acceptance: A turn started by the Claude runtime on an idle session, including a cron-started turn, keeps its foreground root calls attributed to that current runtime and adopted turn for outstanding-work tracking: before, during and after correlated foreground completion it creates no outstanding-work evidence restriction, restricted/lifted notice pair, or orphan-work exclusion window in its own or overlapping peer workspaces. Its edits and tests remain unassigned to Engram grants. This item changes only the host-local outstanding-work hazard classification and notices; it does not implement the Engram unadmitted-turn reporting of w-df1ef323efe9 / w-e12abe9f8cbe, which stays parked on the control-mode decision w-a5cb89d95340.

A one-off foreign observation or mixed-grant mark with no outstanding hazard does not emit an Evidence restricted or subsequent Evidence restriction lifted notice. The affected grant retains its existing mixed-attribution/source-report withholding and any legitimate check fences.

Actual unresolved background, nested or orphaned work still restricts evidence and fences overlapping checks, including across Stop/runtime replacement/deletion; it is released only by the existing correlated-completion rules. Merely hiding a notice never clears an outstanding hazard.

Deterministic source-level regressions drive representative runtime-started frame sequences and inspect hazard/exclusion state while foreground calls are open and after completion, plus true-orphan controls. The exact final input passes authorized focused checks, the full five-stage gate and the independent review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
